{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.5 (Corio / Commerce One Agreement)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side — Corio) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the hosting/licence agreement; verified findings only

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the agreement against our playbook and identified **18 findings**: 2 critical deviations, 2 high-severity items requiring change (1 deviation, 1 missing), 8 medium items (6 deviations, 2 missing), 1 low missing item, 5 compliant positions, and 1 finding that failed verification and is not relied upon below.

The two critical issues are commercial gating items. First, **§ 13.5 (Developments)** flips ownership of interface coding and programs created solely by Corio to Commerce One whenever Commerce One supports them on an ongoing basis, with no licence back — an assignment of our IP to the vendor, and the agreement is silent on non-assignment of Corio and Customer data hosted on the Corio Servers. Second, the **§ 9 liability cap** is nominally mutual but is limited to amounts "actually paid" for "the transaction which the liability relates to", with no US$1,000,000 floor and carve-outs only for § 8; there are no carve-outs for confidentiality/security (§ 10), gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement.

Beyond these, the commercial structure is one-sided on exit and volume: a **five-year initial term terminable only for uncured material breach or insolvency (§ 11.1–11.2)** with no convenience right for us, no post-termination transition assistance or data return mechanic, and an **Exhibit B flat annual MarketSite.net Access Fee** payable across the five years plus a revenue share computed on a deemed minimum of 40 Authorized Software Users per Customer rather than actual usage. The **§ 7.3 warranty period** (60 days from the Effective Date, capped at 31 December 1999) may lapse before Acceptance Testing under § 3.1 concludes, and there is no professional-services warranty. Smaller items: no affiliate/contractor extension of the § 2 licences (despite § 14.8 contemplating subcontracting), § 14.1 assignment gaps, § 4.4 audit mechanics, mandatory AAA arbitration in § 14.3, indemnity scope in § 8, renewal-pricing protection in § 11.1, and no insurance covenant.

Helpfully, several playbook positions are already met with no redline required: no exclusivity obligation on us, no liquidated damages or penalties payable by us, no non-compete or field-of-use covenant binding us, and no MFN burdening us.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue / position |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 13 Shared Resources (§ 13.5) | Ownership of Developments flips to Commerce One where it provides ongoing support, with no licence back; no confirmation that Corio/Customer data is not assigned. Redline: we retain ownership, Commerce One takes a nonexclusive royalty-free support licence, plus data non-assignment confirmation. |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 9 Limitation of Liability | Cap limited to amounts "actually paid" for the related transaction; no US$1m floor; carve-outs only for § 8. Redline: greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and US$1,000,000, mutual, plus Excluded Claims for indemnities, confidentiality/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement. Fallback: straight 12 months' fees with those carve-outs. |
| 3 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § 11 Term and Termination | Five-year initial term with one-year auto-renewals; termination only for uncured material breach or insolvency. Redline: new § 11.4 giving us 30-day convenience right with pro-rata refund and no penalty; confirm Commerce One has no convenience right mid-term. |
| 4 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 3 (Grant of Rights, § 2) | "Affiliate" appears nowhere and no grant names contractors, though § 14.8 contemplates subcontracting and servers may be "operated by or for Corio". Redline: new § 2.11 extending § 2 licences to our affiliates and contractors, with us responsible for compliance. Fallback: affiliate coverage on written notice. |
| 5 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments | Deviation | § 17 Payment Terms / Exhibit B | Flat annual MarketSite.net Access Fee across a five-year term with no reduction or exit right (de facto take-or-pay), and revenue share measured on a deemed 40-user minimum. Redline: 30 days' notice reduction/discontinuation right with pro-rata true-up; revenue share tied to actual Authorized Software Users. |
| 6 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | Deviation | § 8 / § 7 Warranties and Disclaimer (§ 7.3) | 60-day warranty from the Effective Date, capped at 31 December 1999, may expire before or at acceptance under § 3.1; no professional-services warranty. Redline: 12 months from acceptance plus services warranty with re-performance/refund. Fallback: 90 days. |
| 7 | Medium | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | Missing | § 11 Term and Termination | No transition, migration, data export or data-return mechanic; § 12 covers only source code escrow on Release Conditions. Redline: new § 11.4 — up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, data return in a machine-readable format within 30 days, certified deletion thereafter. |
| 8 | Medium | INDEMN — Vendor indemnification | Deviation | § 8 Indemnification | § 8.1 IP indemnity (with § 9 carve-out) is acceptable, but there is no cover for breach of applicable law, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Corio/Customer data, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct. Redline: new § 8.3 adding those heads, using § 8.1 procedure; § 8.2 exclusions untouched. |
| 9 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 14 Miscellaneous (§ 14.3) | California law is acceptable, but mandatory single-arbitrator AAA arbitration in San Francisco is not our forum position; seat is domestic, so medium rather than walk-away. Redline (fallback): retain California law, substitute exclusive jurisdiction of state and federal courts in San Francisco County. |
| 10 | Medium | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 14 Miscellaneous (§ 14.1) | Mutual with an M&A/asset-sale carve-out, but no affiliate carve-out and the direct-competitor exception applies symmetrically, giving Commerce One a consent veto over our own M&A; no reasonableness standard. Redline: affiliate/successor right for us, competitor exception confined to Commerce One assignments, reasonableness standard on consent. |
| 11 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 11 Term and Termination (§ 11.1) | Core position met (12-month renewals, 30-day exit either side), but no vendor renewal reminder and no cap on renewal uplift (Exhibit B leaves "Year 2-5, and beyond" open). Redline: 60-day reminder from Commerce One and renewal increases capped at lesser of CPI and 3%. Fallback: 5%. |
| 12 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 4 Fees (§ 4.4) | Annual frequency, independent CPA reasonably acceptable to us and cost allocation are acceptable; notice is only "reasonable", timing only "reasonable times", no auditor confidentiality undertaking and no bar on systems access. Redline: 30 days' written notice, business hours, confidentiality undertaking, no systems access. |
| 13 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 14 Miscellaneous | No insurance provision despite on-site consultants and professional services (§§ 5.1, 5.2, 5.6) and hosted handling of our and our Customers' data. Redline: new § 14.10 requiring CGL US$1m/2m, E&O US$2m, cyber US$5m, statutory workers' compensation and certificates on request (entire-agreement clause renumbered 14.11). |
| 14 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity on Customer | Compliant | § 3 (Grant of Rights, § 2) | No exclusivity or sole/preferred-source obligation on us; Exhibit D is expressly non-binding. No redline. |
| 15 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 4 Fees | Only ordinary licence, maintenance, access, implementation and revenue-share fees; no stipulated damages, penalties, late interest or termination fee payable by us. No redline. |
| 16 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 13 Shared Resources | No non-compete, field-of-use or post-term restraint binding us; § 13.6 preserves independent development and § 14.8 confirms we direct and may subcontract the services. No redline. |
| 17 | Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | Compliant | Revenue Sharing Fees (Exhibit B) | Pricing and revenue share are fixed figures and percentages; no MFN or price-matching obligation on us. No redline. |
| 18 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Needs review (verification failed) | § 14 Miscellaneous (§ 14.10) | Finding reports no non-solicit/no-hire covenant in the agreement, but verification failed, so we are not relying on it. § 14.10 incorporates a separate NDA and Statement of Work; we should obtain and review those documents for any non-solicit before signature. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

1. **Exhibit B minimum commitment (Finding 5, § 17 Payment Terms).** The flat annual MarketSite.net Access Fee payable on each anniversary across a five-year term exitable only for material breach or insolvency is a de facto multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right — expressly our walk-away position. We need either the 30-day reduction/discontinuation right with true-up or a materially shortened committed period.
2. **Liability cap basis (Finding 2, § 9).** A cap limited to amounts "actually paid" for the single related transaction, with no carve-outs for confidentiality/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement, is not acceptable. Fallback is a straight 12 months' fees cap with the Excluded Claims sentence; we should not sign without at least the carve-outs.
3. **Ownership flip in § 13.5 (Finding 1).** Assignment to Commerce One of work product created solely by us, with no licence back, is not something we can accept. The support-licence construct preserves Commerce One's commercial rationale and should be the landing zone.

For completeness: the arbitration clause (Finding 9) is a medium deviation, **not** a walk-away, because the seat is domestic and California law is on our accepted list.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering Findings 1–13, leading with the three walk-away items and the § 11 exit package (convenience right, transition assistance and data return), which we should present as a single linked ask.
2. **Prioritise negotiation** in this order: § 13.5 ownership → § 9 cap and Excluded Claims → Exhibit B minimum commitment → § 11 exit and transition → § 7.3 warranty period → remaining medium/low items, where the drafted fallbacks give us room to close.
3. **Request the incorporated documents** referenced at § 14.10 (the separate Non-Disclosure Agreement and Statement of Work) and re-run the non-solicitation check (Finding 18), which failed verification; if either contains a non-solicit we will hold it to the mutual, 12-month, directly-involved-personnel fallback with general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire.
4. **Confirm the acceptance-testing timeline** under § 3.1 with the deal team so the § 7.3 warranty extension (12 months from acceptance) is drafted against the actual acceptance date.
5. **Flag the four compliant positions** (Findings 14–17) to the business as items we do not intend to reopen, so we do not spend negotiating capital there.
6. **Route insurance (Finding 13)** to risk management to confirm the CGL/E&O/cyber/workers' compensation levels before we send the covenant, so we can accept a counter without a second round."}
